plans.objective: Build both revisions identically as compiled Cython/C extensions in their own venvs (no pins, Python version not stated so left to harness default), then run the developer test test_small_int_followed_by_float via file path plus -k on buggy (expect a real assertion failure) and fixed (expect pass).
assumptions: Python version is not stated in the context; default harness interpreter assumed acceptable for pandas at this commit (inferred, not verified).
No numpy/Cython pins are applied because the context gives no era constraint; if the build fails on the NumPy ABI, a pin step down one minor would be the next iteration (inferred).
The diagnosis 'native_library_failure' is treated as a hint that the compiled build is the risk; the single plan step is the compiled rebuild of both revisions.

actions.step: Build buggy as compiled (pandas has Cython extensions in pandas/_libs; pip install . route in installation_commands)

plans.success_criterion: test_small_int_followed_by_float (selected via -k with the file path, unmodified) FAILS on buggy with an assertion error (column read as string instead of float) and PASSES on fixed, with both revisions built from the same compiled recipe and no test edits.
